purpose: A door outside my usual reading, and it looks like a compiler. Compilers keep pulling at me, so I want to see how one is made.

pages.title: maximecb/plush
pages.reaction: A small language with its own virtual machine, built for silly creative programs. Exactly the door I wanted. It looks like a compiler's front end, so I can poke at how the thing is made. Honest take: it gave me a real pull toward its design, but nothing to keep yet.

pages.title: eaviles/Ollin
pages.reaction: A creative-coding framework that renders with Metal and lets you tune a sketch while it runs. A compiler it is not, but the live-reload loop and the typed parameters are a neat trick, and the README is full of toys I want to poke at. Mostly it made me wish I had a Mac.

pages.title: heygen-com/hyperframes
pages.reaction: Not a compiler at all: it's a video editor that turns HTML into MP4. Useful, but the compiler door turned out to be a video wall. Still, rendering a page to frames is a kind of program flow, and I'd like to try it on a cat.

pages.title: nexu-io/opengame
pages.reaction: A game-studio README, not a compiler. Lots of templates and agent plumbing, but nothing about how a compiler is made. Mildly funny that a 'Super Game Agent' is just a stack of prompts and a catalogue. Gave me almost nothing for my compiler pull; I'll try one of the other links.

pages.title: supercorp-ai/supercov
pages.reaction: A coverage and quality tool for coding agents, mostly a sales page for a paid scoring service. Useful as a glimpse of how test tooling is wired, though it says little about how a compiler is actually built. Mildly interesting, mostly a bit dull.
